TGDrive modifications to Movi Player 0.4.1, 26 October 2026

Movi Player is Copyright Ujjawal Kashyap and its contributors, licensed under
Apache License 2.0. The original license is distributed alongside this notice
as movi-player-LICENSE.txt. Upstream: https://github.com/mrujjwalg/movi-player

TGDrive modifies the slim JavaScript bundle's seek-completion condition to use
the existing coordinated audio/video buffering path when playable audio is
still priming. This prevents high-latency audio outputs from starting silent
video and then moving the media clock backward when audio arrives. Deliberately
dropped audio, absent/disabled audio and media after the audio tail retain the
upstream behavior.

The exact version and original bundle SHA256 are checked by
website/scripts/patch-movi-player.js. The reviewed modified package is shipped in
website/vendor and installed from that local archive. Normal development and
builds do not rewrite dependencies.
scripts/vendor_viewers.py verifies upstream package integrity and applies the
reviewed recipe only during deliberate vendor regeneration.

TGDrive additionally requires an active audio track before the shared-demux
audio read-ahead branch can bypass video decoder backpressure (2026-10-23).
Video-only previews retain the custom demux/decoder/canvas pipeline.

TGDrive applies the configured HTTP cache budget before load and uses a bounded
window up to that budget, instead of resizing populated buffers after load or
selecting only 8% of medium-sized sources (2026-10-23).

TGDrive separates compressed network read-ahead from decoded frame admission,
targets 90 seconds within the configured byte cap, refills below 75% of that
goal, and scales range requests to the goal. At EOF, hardware decoders drain
pending output instead of taking the HEVC seek-recreation path (2026-10-23).

The compressed source window grows toward its time goal within a device-derived
memory ceiling. Growth preserves retained data and stream state; background
writers refresh storage after awaited reads. Allocation failure retains the
existing window and caps subsequent growth for the opening (2026-10-23).

The read-ahead gate counts bytes only within the current source window. Distant
seeks do not count the skipped file gap as already buffered, allowing the first
range at the new position to arrive before the demuxer advances (2026-10-23).

The decoder EOF drain is bounded and ignores obsolete decoder generations.
In-flight demuxer reads can receive their required byte range without being
blocked by the speculative read-ahead target. Native chapter navigation uses
chapter titles and times without extracting frames unless thumbnails or a
storyboard are explicitly enabled (2026-10-26).

Disconnecting the native element revokes picked subtitle Blob URLs and clears
their ownership list, including when source reset and disconnect both run
(2026-10-26).

Revision 0.4.1-tgdrive.2 (2026-10-28) escapes media track metadata in settings
and context menus; unregisters element-owned global listeners, recurring UI
timers and owned media-session actions on disconnect; and makes preview waits
cancellable. Audio-only containers no longer wait for video frames. Software EOF
drains queued packets and delayed frames through the existing decoder ABI before
reset; seek/reset generations invalidate obsolete drains. Decoded-picture queue
targets account for device/pixel costs, and statistics distinguish WebCodecs from
verified hardware acceleration. Chapter cards remain immediate; TGDrive fills
only visible chapter images. Preview initialization requires a viewer request.
The decoder WASM and upstream licenses remain unchanged.

Revision 0.4.1-tgdrive.3 (2026-10-28) removes demux-cursor peak sampling from
speculative read-ahead and reduces pause-time targets to a small resume cushion.
Thumbnail byte ranges can be reused by the same playback source through a bounded
cache without repositioning its active window. Source identity and complete byte
coverage are required before reuse. New image operations have a bounded allowance
for thumbnail range requests, including initialization and retries; cached reads
remain available after the allowance is exhausted. The decoder WASM is unchanged.
